explainer_content.short_definition: Acoustic song as public argument, community memory, and movement language.
explainer_content.history_capsule: The folk revival drew from older ballads, labor songs, blues, gospel, and topical writing, then placed them in coffeehouses, festivals, campuses, and civil-rights contexts.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It made the songwriter a public witness and gave later rock, country-folk, and singer-songwriter music a moral vocabulary.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: The performance often sounds deliberately plain so the words and group participation stay central.
